What really drives our growth, and what should we do next? Help us find out.
Why does a customer turn down an offer that would save them money? Which product should we launch next? In what marketing channel should we scale spend? You’ll ask the right questions, find the answers, put a number on them and make sure we act.
If you want your analysis to shape where we grow, we should talk.
The foundation is built. Now it needs to grow.
Anyfin helps people pay less for the loans they already have. We only make an offer if we can lower someone's total cost. Since 2017 we've helped people across Sweden, Finland and Germany take back control of their finances. We're profitable, we have a banking licence that lets us operate across the EU, and we're getting ready to launch new products and enter new markets. Our ambition is to be a pan-European company by 2030.
Every one of those steps raises a question: which product, which market, which change to the customer journey makes the biggest difference? Growing well depends on answering them properly.
The team is small and intentionally so. We'd rather have fewer people who care about doing things properly and move fast because they trust each other. If you join, you won't disappear into a big org. You'll shape what we build and where we go next.
The actual job
You'll join our Commercial team within Growth and work across both business and product. One week you're digging into why customers drop off in the app. Next you're building the case for a new product or market.
You'll own the funnel. That covers web and app, from first visit to payout. You'll find where and why customers drop off, put a number on the opportunity and recommend what to fix first.
You'll come up with new bets. These could be new products, features, loyalty or cross-sell. You'll build the business case, test it and tell us whether it's worth pursuing.
You'll work out what brings customers back. That means understanding how customer value grows over time and what we can do to grow it.
You'll help shape decisions. You'll present clear recommendations to teams and management, helping them understand the opportunity, the trade-offs and what we should do next.
Analysis in an AI-native company
AI isn't a side tool here. It's built into how we work across engineering, analytics, operations and product, and our tech team has built an AI-connected data and code environment on frontier models.
For an analyst, that means you can go further and faster than before. You can write queries, explore data and test hypotheses with tools like Claude at your side. It also means more answers that sound confident and might be wrong.
Part of this role is knowing the difference. We want someone who uses AI to go deeper, and who still questions the data, the assumptions and the AI-generated answer before drawing a conclusion.
The people
You'll work closely with people who enjoy getting into a problem and figuring out what to do about it. They're generous with what they know, quick to laugh and happy to change their minds when they learn something new.
You'll have room to take initiative and people to think things through with. Some ideas will work, others won't. We try things, learn from the results and use that to make the next decision better.
This sounds like you if…
You have an MSc in engineering, business, finance or a similar quantitative field.
You have experience in product, growth or business analytics, ideally in a consumer business. You write strong SQL, and you know how to design an A/B test and how to tell when one is lying to you.
You can take an open question all the way to a clear recommendation. You connect product metrics to what actually happens for customers and to what it's worth for the business.
You're hungry and curious, and you want to own real problems rather than answer someone else's tickets.
We care more about what you can do, your judgment and your drive than a specific number of years. Experience in fintech or consumer lending is a plus, and so is Swedish, Finnish or German. Fluent English is required.
More than anything, you can tell us about an analysis that changed what a company did. Not just what you found, but what happened because of it.
A few practical notes
You’ll be based at our office on Drottninggatan 92 in Stockholm. We work from the office because we value the collaboration, shared learning and team spirit that come from spending time together.
We interview on a rolling basis and would love for you to join us as soon as possible. EU work authorisation is required.
Want to see your analysis turn into real improvements for our customers? We’d love to hear from you.

About Multiply & VisFlow
Multiply is a technology-driven end-to-end solution provider operating at the intersection of advanced software development, system engineering and data-driven platforms. Together with VisFlow — our proprietary product for structured, visual and traceable technical knowledge — we help organizations build, operate and continuously evolve complex systems within security-critical and data-intensive domains.
VisFlow transforms complex technical processes, system flows and operational knowledge into clear, visual and interconnected representations. The platform enables teams to understand, manage and scale advanced systems throughout their entire lifecycle — from development and deployment to operations and continuous improvement.

These roles are suited for engineers who enjoy working close to the technology, combining structured engineering methods with hands-on problem-solving in multidisciplinary environments.

Current Focus Areas

Supporting hardware prototype integration and hands-on testing

Capturing test results and technical feedback to refine design and system requirements

Collaborating with internal teams, suppliers and external stakeholders
Contributing to structured documentation, traceability and lifecycle governance

You will be responsible for ensuring that development, integration and verification activities can be carried out efficiently, structurally and with high quality.
Typical responsibilities may include:
Establishing, developing and maintaining lab environments and reference systems
Designing and implementing modular test solutions, integration rigs and test equipment

Contributing to integration, verification and validation strategies
Ensuring strong configuration management, structure and traceability in test environments

Collaborating with development teams, delivery projects and other technical functions

You may have experience from defence, aerospace, rail, radio communications, med-tech, telecom, automotive, industrial systems or other sectors with high demands on robustness, reliability, traceability and quality.

Experience with requirements management and systems engineering processes

jobs.description:
Advancing specialty steel through research and innovation 
From metallurgical research to real-world applicationsDeveloping specialty steel for demanding applications requires a deep understanding of materials, a curiosity to investigate complex problems and the ability to turn scientific findings into practical solutions. At Ovako, this also means working with customers to understand their challenges and exploring how steel can help them develop new products, improve performance and bring new ideas to life. 
As a leading European producer of specialty steel, Ovako combines more than 300 years of industrial expertise with modern technology and a strong commitment to sustainability. As part of Nippon Steel, the company also benefits from an international network of metallurgical knowledge. 
Ovako is looking for a Senior R&D Engineer with expertise in alloy design and materials performance to strengthen its R&D organisation in Hofors, Sweden. 
This role offers the opportunity to combine advanced metallurgical research with customer-driven industrial development. You will investigate how steel composition and processing influence material properties, develop new alloy concepts and tackle complex challenges arising from real applications. Working closely with customers and sales, you will help translate specific performance requirements into material solutions, gaining insight into a range of industries and seeing how your research contributes to customers’ development journeys. 
About the roleAs a Senior R&D Engineer, you will drive research activities in alloy design, steel development and materials performance, combining computational modelling, experimental investigations and collaboration with external research partners. 
Approximately 60% of your time will be dedicated to customer projects. You will investigate material behaviour, assess application requirements and develop steel solutions to meet demanding performance needs. The challenges will vary across applications and industries, giving you the opportunity to apply your scientific expertise to a broad range of practical problems. You will also support product development at Ovako’s production mills, helping connect customer requirements, material performance and industrial processes. 
Collaboration with universities and research institutes is an important part of the role, alongside participation in nationally and internationally funded research projects. You will have opportunities to expand your technical network through research partnerships, conferences and occasional travel to research institutes and other Ovako sites in Europe. 
Your responsibilities 
Developing new steel grades and alloy concepts, from composition to processing route 
Computational alloy design using Thermo-Calc and related tools 
Planning and evaluating corrosion testing data and hydrogen embrittlement investigations 
Driving nationally and internationally funded research projects and consortia 
Collaborating with universities and institutes, including supervision of students 
Supporting sales and customers with qualified answers on material behaviour and selection 
Identifying new research directions that strengthen Ovako's product portfolio and long-term competitiveness 

The position is placed in Hofors, Sweden, with possibilities to work 2 days a week from home.  
Your profileYou are a scientifically driven metallurgist or materials scientist who enjoys exploring the mechanisms behind material behaviour and applying research to complex industrial challenges. You are motivated by understanding why materials behave the way they do and using that knowledge to develop solutions to problems without obvious answers. 
We are looking for someone with: 
A PhD in metallurgy or materials science, with a strong focus on steels and metallic materials. 
At least three years of research experience after your PhD, gained at a university, company R&D centre or research institute. 
Documented expertise in steel alloy design, including hands-on experience with Thermo-Calc. 
Excellent communication skills in English and the ability to explain complex technical findings to different audiences, including customers. 

You should also have experience in nationally or internationally funded research collaborations. 
Meritorious experience:Experience from research or development projects related to corrosion of metallic materials and hydrogen embrittlement of steels is considered an advantage, as these topics represent important current and future challenges within several of Ovako’s research collaborations and customer-driven development projects. 
Who are you?You are curious, analytical and persistent in your approach to research. You enjoy challenging established assumptions, investigating mechanisms and building the evidence needed to understand complex materials problems. 
You combine scientific rigour with a collaborative mindset. You communicate clearly, share knowledge and work effectively with colleagues, customers, production teams and external research partners. 
Ovako's core values are Innovative, Skilled and Responsible. The company looks for people who demonstrate these values through their expertise, curiosity and commitment to continuous improvement. 
Why Ovako?At Ovako, you will work with advanced specialty steel in an environment where scientific research meets real industrial challenges. You will collaborate with experienced specialists, customers, universities and research institutes, with opportunities to deepen your expertise and contribute to the development of future steel solutions. 
As part of Nippon Steel, you will also benefit from an international network of metallurgical knowledge and research collaboration.

Right now, we are looking for a Process Engineer – Direct Reduction for our Green Iron Operations. The team is responsible for optimizing process performance, supporting safe and stable operations, and driving continuous improvements across our hydrogen production and direct reduction plants.
Specific to this role, the day-to-day tasks will include the following, but as we are a growing company with very few silos between teams, other tasks might be included as well.

Provide day-to-day process engineering support to ensure safe, stable, and efficient plant operations.

Monitor plant performance, troubleshoot process upsets, and lead root cause analyses to improve reliability and operational excellence.

Optimize process performance through process modelling, heat and mass balances, debottlenecking, and energy efficiency initiatives.

Support direct reduction operations during commissioning, start-ups, shutdowns, and operational changes.

Review and develop engineering documentation, including PFDs, P&IDs, process calculations, SOPs, and process control strategies.

Collaborate with Operations, Maintenance, Automation, and OEM partners to improve process performance and implement engineering solutions.

Drive continuous improvement projects, monitor production KPIs, and prepare technical reports to support data-driven decision-making.

Promote safe operations by supporting process safety activities, hydrogen safety standards, PTW/LOTO compliance, and technical training.

What you'll bring
You're curious and believe that real progress happens when we work together. You're not afraid to challenge old ways of thinking—and you treat others with respect while doing it. At Stegra, we value people who take initiative, build trust, and help create a workplace where everyone can do their best.
Specific to this role, we'd like to see that you bring:

A degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or another relevant engineering discipline.

Solid process engineering experience from an operating, commercial-scale Direct Reduction plant.

Experience supporting commissioning, start-ups, process optimization, or operational improvements in an industrial setting.

A strong understanding of process engineering fundamentals, with the ability to analyse complex systems and turn insights into practical solutions.

Experience with hydrogen production is a plus. Curiosity about the hydrogen process and a willingness to learn are important.

Confidence working across disciplines and collaborating with Operations, Maintenance, Automation, Engineering, and external partners to achieve shared goals.

A proactive, structured, and safety-first approach, with a continuous improvement mindset.

Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken. Swedish is an advantage but not a requirement.

Benefits at Stegra 
At Stegra, you’ll join a company where your work has real impact on the climate, the industry, and future generations. We’re building a culture rooted in safety, trust, and inclusion, where people feel supported to grow and thrive.
You’ll receive fair, competitive compensation aligned with collective agreements, along with benefits like up to 30 days of paid vacation, occupational pension, parental benefits, and insurance. If you need support with relocation or immigration, our relocation department will help guide you through the process, whether it’s permits, housing or other practical matters. You can also enjoy perks like subsidized gym memberships and bike leases, plus the everyday benefits of life closer to nature.
Read more about Benefits at Stegra here.
This is Stegra
Stegra is on a mission to change the global steel industry by producing green hydrogen, iron, and steel - with the goal of eliminating CO₂ emissions. Instead of coal, we use green hydrogen and fossil-free electricity, meaning our primary emissions will be water and heat.
By 2030, our ambition is to produce 5 million tonnes of green steel annually in our fully integrated, digitized, and sustainable plant in Boden, Northern Sweden - currently under construction. But this is just the beginning. Our expertise in green hydrogen will enable us to decarbonize industries beyond steel, paving the way for a cleaner future.
Our Boden Site
Our Boden site is located just west of Boden City, right in the heart of a growing green industrial hub in Northern Sweden. It’s where we’re building one of the world’s most modern, sustainable steel plants—designed with safety, efficiency, and people in mind. With just a 10-minute commute from town, you'll be close to both cutting-edge technology and the everyday convenience of living near nature, schools, and community life.

The department's activities are conducted at two main locations: Natrium on Medicinaregatan 7B in Gothenburg, and the Kristineberg Marine Research Station in Fiskebäckskil. The current position is located at the premises in Gothenburg, which is where Herbarium GB is situated. The latter hosts more than one million specimens from around the world (~60% imaged; ~28% with digitized metadata) and forms part of a global network of almost 4,000 herbaria.
Subject area 
Botany, specializing in vascular plant systematics.
Subject area description 
Vascular plant systematics is the scientific study of the diversity, evolutionary relationships, and taxonomy of vascular plants. In the 21st century, systematics is a highly integrative discipline, one that engages a diversity of data types and methodologies, and has strong connections to evolutionary biology, ecology, and conservation biology. For this position we seek a plant systematist having competence in the tools of modern systematics, a strong interest in natural history collections, and whose research makes first-hand use of material housed in such collections.
 
Duties 
This associate senior lectureship initially comprises 60% research and teaching in botany and 40% curation of the vascular plant collections at Herbarium GB. The curation component comprises contribution to strategic development of the collections, basic curation, and curation-related research.
Teaching and research tasks include:
Development of and engagement with a sustained, substantive, and productive research program focusing on vascular plants. A significant component of the research should be collections-based, making use of herbarium material.
Building and leading a research group, including applying for external research funding and publishing in high-quality scientific journals.
Teaching topics in plant taxonomy, systematics, and related subjects at undergraduate and graduate levels. This includes lecturing, coordination of practical exercises, course leadership, and project supervision.
Supervising doctoral students.
Participation in the development and renewal of teaching, in both content and form.
Development of collaborations with other research groups at University of Gothenburg and with researchers at other institutions. The department is especially keen to strengthen its collaboration with the Gothenburg Botanical Garden, with respect to research, teaching, and collection management.
Participation in and development of societal collaboration projects.

Curation tasks include:
Participation in the development of strategic goals and drafting of grant applications for Herbarium GB.
Curation and development of the vascular plant collections in Herbarium GB.
Execution and publication of research relating to or arising from curation activities.
Promoting integration of Herbarium GB into university- and botanic garden-based teaching, research, and community activities.
Support of digitization and database cataloguing in line with international standards for specimen data.
Support of visiting researchers and promoting collaboration with national and international institutions.

 
Eligibility 
Eligibility for employment as an associate senior lecturer is regulated by the Higher Education Ordinance and the University of Gothenburg's employment regulations.
To be eligible for appointment as an associate senior lecturer, the applicant must have been awarded a PhD or has the corresponding research expertise. Primary consideration should be given to a person who has been awarded a PhD or achieved the equivalent expertise within seven years of the deadline for application for employment as an associate senior lecturer. However, a person who has been awarded a PhD or achieved equivalent expertise at an earlier date may also be considered if there are exceptional circumstances. Exceptional circumstances are sick leave, parental leave, or other similar circumstances. 
Ability to teach in English is a requirement.
Assessment criteria 
The assessment criteria for appointment as associate senior lecturer are governed by the Higher Education Ordinance and the Appointments Procedure for Teachers at the University of Gothenburg. We seek candidates who have demonstrated the ability to independently initiate, develop, and conduct high-quality research within the subject area of the position. For appointment as an associate senior lecturer at the Faculty of Science and Technology, academic and teaching qualifications must be adequate in relation to the subject content and job description of the advertised position.
For this position, emphasis is placed on research qualifications and expertise, particularly in herbarium specimen-based research, with curation skills considered to be of similar importance. The assessment categories of collaboration with the wider community and management and administrative expertise are considered advantageous.
The assessment of research and curation skills includes
Proficiency in vascular plant systematics, taxonomy, and nomenclature, as evidenced by publications and participation in scientific conferences.
Experience of herbarium curation and/or collections-based taxonomic research.
Advanced knowledge of modern techniques in taxonomy and systematics, including phylogenetic and phylogenomic tools.
A clear vision of the future role and operation of herbaria, and thoughts on the priority actions required to realize that vision.
Experience of herbarium digitization, georeferencing, and/or database development.
Knowledge of the Northern Eurasian and/or Eurasian floras, specifically floristics and regional plant identification.

Personal qualities such as initiative, organization skills, pedagogical insight, and communication skills will also be taken into consideration..
Employment 
Type of employment: Fixed-term employment for five years
Extent: Full-time (100%)
Location: Gothenburg
Starting date: By agreement

jobs.occupation: Electronics Engineer to Hardware Department at Westermo
jobs.description:
Do you want to develop robust electronics used in mission-critical applications? Join Westermo's Hardware Department and as our new Electronics Engineer!
Are you passionate about electronics design and looking for a role where you can follow your work from idea to finished product?
At Westermo, we develop and manufacture industrial data communication solutions used in critical infrastructure worldwide. As an Electronics Engineer, you will be part of our Hardware Department, developing the robust, high-quality products that have made Westermo a trusted global supplier.

Are you our next Electronics Engineer?
You will join our Hardware Department and become part of a team of eight Electronics Engineers. We work across the entire product life cycle, from requirements and design to production and customer value.

Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or similar

Experience in electronics hardware design

Fluent in English, both written and spoken

Proficient in Swedish, both written and spoken

Meritorious

Experience developing industrial products or products used in demanding environments

Experience in design for manufacturing (DFM) and design for test (DFT)

Experience working closely with production

You will be working at the forefront of technology in a friendly, open culture where we you get the opportunity to learn from skilled colleagues every day. A mature and caring leadership in a flat organization. Through our collective bargain agreement, you will be covered in terms of insurance, pension, and other benefits. We are a learning organization, and we truly love to try new things, think outside the box and be innovative together!

Location: Kopparlunden, Västerås

Job type: Full time

Employment contract: Permanent

For questions about the role, please contact Recruiting Manager Mikael Lindeborg; mikael.lindeborg@westermo.com or Recruiter Elin Sandell; elin.sandell@westermo.com

jobs.occupation: Director Research Programs & Consortia  Medical Imaging
jobs.description:
Are you a business-minded research professional with deep expertise in medical imaging who thrives in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment?
Do you enjoy combining scientific and technical expertise with commercial understanding, taking ownership and driving complex research collaborations towards successful outcomes?
Collective Minds is looking for a Director, Research Programs & Consortia to drive our portfolio of public and private research collaborations. This is a broad, hands-on role with significant responsibility and the opportunity to make a real impact in a growing international healthtech company.
About Collective Minds
Collective Minds is based in Stockholm/Danderyd and we operate globally across clinical trials and life sciences. We are an imaging platform for clinical trials that connects hospitals, experts, and industry - including CROs, pharma, biotech, medtech, and eClinical vendors - enabling trials with imaging endpoints and the generation of high-quality evidence faster and more efficiently. We are a fast-moving, commercially minded team focused on collaboration, accountability, and impact. By combining deep domain expertise in medical imaging with novel cloud technology, we help customers reduce risk, ensure compliance, accelerate and scale research.
About the role
As Director, Research Programs & Consortia, you will take responsibility for our portfolio of more than 10 public and private research consortia, which are a key part of Collective Minds' strategy and ongoing delivery.
Working alongside CROs, biotech and medtech companies, pharmaceutical partners, academic hospitals and research organizations, these collaborations span medical imaging, big data, analytics, and AI modeling and validation across therapeutic areas such as oncology, immunology, cardiovascular and musculoskeletal research.
Within these projects, Collective Minds acts as a data manager and platform provider, bringing deep expertise in medical imaging to support complex research collaborations.

Drive the research project portfolio, ensuring successful delivery within agreed budgets, timelines, scope and commitments.
Coordinate project and research managers, aligning priorities, following up on progress and ensuring accountability across projects.
Personally manage selected research consortia, including scientific, technical and operational activities.
Provide scientific and technical guidance across medical imaging, data analytics, AI modeling and validation.
Ensure effective use of the Collective Minds platform, prioritizing standardized and scalable solutions over unnecessary custom development.
Manage budgets, project scope and stakeholder expectations, balancing scientific objectives with commercial priorities.
Ensure accurate reporting to customers, funders and partners, including grant deliverables and efficient project close-outs.
Collaborate with clinical and technical operations teams to plan capacity, resolve challenges and continuously improve project delivery.

We are looking for a scientifically experienced and business-minded professional who combines deep expertise in medical imaging with a strong track record of delivering complex research projects.
You are analytical, pragmatic and comfortable working independently in a fast-moving environment. You enjoy collaborating across disciplines, making decisions and finding effective solutions without adding unnecessary complexity.
You communicate clearly, build trust with internal and external stakeholders and know how to balance scientific quality with business priorities and efficient execution.
We believe you have:
A strong scientific background in life sciences, medical sciences, biomedical engineering or a related field, with deep expertise in medical imaging research.
Experience from a commercial life sciences, medtech, biotech, pharma, CRO or healthtech environment, including scientific and academic collaborations.
Proven experience managing complex research programs or consortia, including budgets, timelines, scope, reporting and project close-outs.
Hands-on experience with research consortia, work package delivery, grant writing, grant execution and funding-related reporting.
Strong technical skills, including scientific programming, analytical tools and data-driven research workflows.
The ability to assess complex scientific and technical requirements, make informed decisions and contribute to technical implementations when needed.
Commercial awareness and the ability to balance scientific objectives with budgets, resources and project commitments.
Strong communication, coordination and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to drive results across teams and external partners.
A proactive, hands-on and solution-oriented approach, with the ability to adapt quickly and take initiative.
Fluency in English, both written and spoken.
Willingness to travel internationally as required by research projects, typically approximately every two months.
Ability to work regularly from our Stockholm/Danderyd office.

Why join Collective Minds?
At Collective Minds, you will join an innovative and ambitious company where technology, science and collaboration come together to make a meaningful difference in healthcare.
You will be part of an entrepreneurial environment with short decision-making processes, engaged colleagues and the opportunity to influence how things are done.
This is an opportunity to take responsibility for a strategically important research portfolio, work with leading scientific and industry partners and contribute to the continued growth of an international healthtech company.
We look forward to receiving your application!

At Galderma, we advance dermatology for every skin story. As the category leader in dermatology, we bring together science, innovation and people who are passionate about making a meaningful difference for patients around the world.

Experience conducting risk assessments and applying Quality Risk Management principles.
Experience supporting audits, inspections and regulatory compliance activities.

Location and information

Why Galderma
At Galderma, you'll have the opportunity to work in a science-driven, innovative, and collaborative environment where quality and patient impact are at the center of everything we do. You'll join a team of talented colleagues and play an important role in supporting the continued growth of our biologics and protein-based portfolio.

They say, “it’s not rocket science.” We disagree.
Welcome to SSC Space (formerly Swedish Space Corporation), the perfect workplace for those passionate about technology in general and space in particular.  
With space organizations, research institutes, institutional and commercial actors as customers, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications, spacecraft consulting services, rocket and balloon systems, and much more. 
SSC Space also has one of the world’s largest global networks of ground stations for satellite communications. We own and operate the Esrange Space Center in Kiruna, northern Sweden, with the aim of launching satellites in the near future. 
We are now looking for an AWS DevOps Engineer who will build and improve the infrastructure and deployment workflows that support our systems. Working across AWS and on-premises environments, you will help developers deliver software reliably, strengthen security through automated controls and make our systems easier to operate and monitor. 

JOB REQUIREMENTS
We are looking for someone who enjoys solving practical problems through automation and takes ownership of system reliability. You work well across IT and development teams, share your knowledge and look for ways to make everyday operations better.
You bring:
At least three years of hands-on AWS experience in production environments.
Practical experience with infrastructure as code, using tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, AWS CodePipeline or Jenkins.
Experience managing Kubernetes clusters in cloud or on-premises environments.
Fluency in Swedish and English, both spoken and written.

Experience with Ansible or similar configuration management tools, scripting in Python or Bash, and DevOps practices is an advantage.
Swedish citizenship is required for this role.
 
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES
You will work closely with developers, architects and IT colleagues to improve how we build, deploy and manage our environments.
Your responsibilities include:
Develop and maintain infrastructure as code using tools such as Terraform and CloudFormation, and automate configuration with Ansible.
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for cloud-based systems and applications.
Automate deployments and environment provisioning to improve consistency and reduce manual work.
Manage containerized workloads in Amazon EKS and on-premises Kubernetes environments.
Develop monitoring and observability across cloud and on-premises resources using Grafana and application performance monitoring tools.
Investigate operational incidents and improve reliability through testing, automation and lessons learned.
Build security policies and automated guardrails into infrastructure and deployment workflows.
Manage software artefacts and container images using Amazon ECR and JFrog, supporting a secure software supply chain.
Contribute to solution design, quality assurance and clear documentation of infrastructure and processes for internal use and audits.

 
BENEFITS
We offer you 
A unique opportunity to contribute to a wide range of projects and play an active role in both the Swedish and international space industry. 
An excellent opportunity for personal and career development. 
An exciting, international workplace characterized by an open atmosphere and proud employees all over the world.  

You will work with colleagues across engineering and IT, develop your skills across cloud and on-premises environments, and contribute to how we build and operate our systems.
 Additional benefits 
In addition to vacation and traditional public holidays, we offer extra paid leave throughout the year, such as time off between Christmas and New Year, Ascension Day, amounting to 6-11 extra days depending on the calendar.  
Wellness allowance of SEK 5,000 per year. 
Health benefits such as voluntary health insurance and regular health checks for eligible employees.  
Access to a benefit bike through a tax-efficient leasing program. 
Support for employee-driven activities that promote connection, health, and culture across teams. 
Collective Agreement, including good pensions plans, parental pay and insurance. 

 
LOCATION
This is a full-time, permanent position based at our office in Solna Strand. 
 
NEXT STEP
If this opportunity sparks your interest, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible! We review applications continuously and will conduct interviews throughout the process. 
Please note, however, that the position may be filled before this date, and the advertisement may therefore close earlier. This allows us to manage the process efficiently and give each application the attention it deserves. 
When applying, please include your CV. While you are welcome to include a brief personal note or letter, our evaluation will primarily focus on your skills and qualifications as outlined in your CV, ensuring a fair and unbiased recruitment process.  
As part of our recruitment process, all candidates selected for employment undergo a background check and security screening. Citizenship requirements may apply depending on the role. 
 
WE HELP EARTH BENEFIT FROM SPACE
SSC Space is a leading global provider of advanced space services, with more than 50 years of experience. We help space organizations, research institutes, commercial and institutional actors from all over the world to get access to space. 
With local presence on all continents and about 800 committed employees, we offer specialist expertise in satellite communications and satellite control services, spacecraft operations, rocket and balloon systems, launch services and flight test services, as well as engineering, operations and consultancy services for space missions. 
We help Earth benefit from Space. Learn more at sscspace.com

Gasometer is set to open in spring 2027 in Norra Djurgårdsstaden, Stockholm, establishing itself as a new destination where culture, gastronomy, and live experiences come together. Housed within an iconic industrial building, Gasometer will become a venue for world-class productions, events, and unforgettable experiences.
Here, food and beverage are not simply complementary elements, but an essential part of the overall guest experience. Renowned chef Stefan Eriksson leads the culinary direction, with menus built around seasonal ingredients, responsible sourcing, and close partnerships with carefully selected producers. Better on the plate. Better for what comes after.
We are now looking for two Sous Chefs who want to be part of building something extraordinary from the ground up. This is an opportunity to help shape a destination where food, beverage, culture, and live experiences come together to create unforgettable moments for our guests.
Your Responsibilities
As a Sous Chef, you will work closely with the Head Chef and play a key role in the daily operation of the kitchen. You will lead the team during service and ensure that every dish leaving the kitchen meets the highest standards of quality, both in taste and presentation.
Our operation covers everything from intimate private dining experiences to large-scale events and productions. No two days are the same, requiring flexibility, dedication, and a genuine passion for food and hospitality.
As a Sous Chef, You Will

Work across both hot and cold kitchen sections, participating in preparation and service

Lead, coach, and motivate the kitchen team during service

Ensure quality, presentation, and compliance with established procedures

Plan orders and purchasing together with the Head Chef

Contribute to menu development and operational planning

Maintain structure, organization, and high hygiene standards throughout the kitchen

Collaborate closely with other departments to deliver a world-class guest experience

Be a part of our educational program for the whole team

We Are Looking for Someone Who Has

At least 2 years of experience working as a Sous Chef

Previous experience in large-scale event, arena, or high-volume operations is considered an advantage

Strong English language skills and the ability to understand Swedish in a kitchen environment

A genuine interest in sustainable cooking and responsible sourcing

A keen eye for detail, organization, and quality

We are looking for someone who is passionate, driven, and confident in their leadership. You have a genuine interest in gastronomy and thrive in an environment where the pace can be demanding at times, but where quality is never compromised. Also love to cook perfect bouillons, slowly simmer, skim, sieve and reduce and transform it to a beautiful sauce!
You are solution-oriented, structured, and able to remain calm under pressure. At the same time, you are a team player who values collaboration and contributes to a positive and supportive work environment.
Why join us?
This is an opportunity for someone who wants to be part of building something from the ground up. You will join a business with high ambitions, a clear vision, and a long-term perspective, where collaboration is at the heart of everything we do and every role contributes to the bigger picture.
We believe great workplaces start with fair conditions, which is why we offer collective bargaining coverage and competitive employee benefits.
This is a full-time, permanent position with a preferred start date of 11 January, or by agreement. A probationary period applies. Evening and weekend work is part of the role. You will report to the Head chef.
Collective bargaining agreements and competitive employment benefits are a given for us.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so don't wait to apply.
As part of your application, we would like you to include a motivation letter explaining what attracts you to the Sous Chef role. The motivation letter replaces the traditional cover letter and can either be included directly in your CV or uploaded under "Cover Letter."
About Gasometer & Miramis
Gasometer is part of Miramis, a hospitality group operating hotels, restaurants, and event venues across Italy and Sweden.
Everything we build is centered around experiences and meaningful connections. We believe joy can be found in many different moments: at a rock concert, during an evening walk, around a memorable dinner table, or through an unexpected encounter in a small fishing village. We grow by listening to both guests and colleagues, and by understanding the history and heritage of the places where we operate. There are no one-size-fits-all solutions. Every location, every guest, and every day is unique.
Today, Miramis owns five properties along the southern coast of Tuscany and owns or operates an additional four properties in Stockholm. What unites them is their deep connection to place. Each project carries a social and cultural heritage that we continue to develop through creative energy, contemporary design, local engagement, and a sustainable approach to hospitality.

Location: Stockholm, Sweden
We prefer a candidate who can work from our headquarters in Stockholm. For a strong candidate we are however willing to consider work from a home office in Denmark, Norway or Finland.
About the position
As an Application & Physics Specialist you will join a diverse and dedicated specialist group with clinical experience from different countries. The group is part of the global service organization responsible for the promotion, deployment and support of our products as well as the education of our customers.  
The emphasis of the position will be on working with potential and current customers in the Nordic region to introduce them to our treatment planning system RayStation through demonstrations and training. For a candidate with medical physics competence, you will also play an important role in assisting our customers during the beam commissioning process, for example by creating beam models and advising them on measurement requirements.

Your main tasks
Planning, performing and documenting product trainings for customers and distributors
Demonstrating RaySearch products at trade shows and onsite for prospective customers
Develop and maintain training materials
Answering tenders and explain product functionality
Collaborating with our development department through exploratory testing of new product versions 
Assisting and guiding customers during the beam commissioning process

Your introduction

Your profile
We believe that our new Application & Physics Specialist has a great sense for service and customer support and a strong motivation to work in a highly dynamic environment. You are a social and positive person with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and enjoy presenting and teaching to bigger and smaller crowds. 
Further, you can quickly adapt to new contexts and appreciate various environments as well as a variety of different tasks.  You enjoy facing new challenges and solving complex problems, both independently and in collaboration with your team members. You are comfortable with working proactively, taking initiatives and have the ability to prioritize your work and adapt to sudden changes. 
Experience & skills
Proficiency in spoken and written English
Swedish/Danish/Norwegian/Finnish skills are meriting
BSc or MSc degree in medical physics/dosimetry/RTT or equivalent, medical physics is meriting
Clinical experience in radiotherapy, especially proton therapy or brachytherapy, is meriting
Ability to travel up to 25% 
Medical device industry experience is meriting

Our culture
Culture at RaySearch is the driving force behind our organization, where everything we do is driven by a shared passion for innovation and the fight against cancer. Our dedication is reflected in our ability to deliver exceptional results, pay close attention to detail, and consistently go the extra mile. Our employees stand out as experts in their field, driven by a relentless focus on solving problems - no matter how complex. At RaySearch, we take pride in leading the way in cancer treatment, leveraging cutting-edge technology to develop innovative solutions that make a real difference in patient care.
Our offer
At RaySearch, we offer a diverse and inclusive work environment, fostering openness, sincerity, and collaboration. Located in Hagastaden, Stockholm's Life Science Hub, our modern and creative workspace includes an in-house gym, yoga, and social activities like ping pong, table football, and regular after-work events. Our bistro serves a fantastic lunch buffet, and we offer morning- and afternoon-fika every day. Our rooftop terrace also provides a stunning 360-degree view of Stockholm, enhancing the work experience. All of this comes attached with a competitive compensation and benefits package.
Application

TL;DR
We're looking for an exceptional AI Software Engineer to build the AI-powered People systems that help Lovable scale.
As Lovable grows, we're rethinking how work gets done. Rather than relying on traditional HR software, we're building AI-native products that transform hiring, onboarding, workforce planning, identity, compliance, and other core People workflows.
You'll work embedded with our People team, partnering closely with stakeholders to understand problems, design solutions, and ship production-ready software. Many of the products you build won't stop at improving Lovable internally — they have the potential to become capabilities we offer to customers in the future, giving you the opportunity to shape products that start inside Lovable and scale far beyond it.
Why Lovable?
Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.
We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.
Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.
Why join now?
Very few engineering roles offer this level of ownership.
You'll help define how AI transforms internal operations. You'll work directly with the People team to identify problems, design solutions, and build products that improve how Lovable operates every day.
As Lovable scales, we're building the operating system the company runs on—function by function, directly in Lovable. The People team is one of the first. You'll help define how AI transforms one of our most important internal functions, and the best ideas will eventually become building blocks for our customers.
What we're looking for
We're looking for a software engineer with strong product instincts and experience building secure software that handles sensitive information.
You'll likely have:
Experience shipping production software that handles sensitive data — HR tech, fintech, identity management, or similar.
Experience working with people data, business systems, analytics platforms, or enterprise data infrastructure (e.g. BigQuery, Snowflake, Databricks, Airflow, Fivetran, SQL, etc.).
Deep familiarity with HR systems and/or ATS platforms (HiBob, Ashby, Workday, Greenhouse, or similar), either as a builder or through close collaboration with People teams.
Experience designing secure systems with role-based access control and data permissioning.
Strong product instincts—you think end-to-end, ask why, and care about building products people actually use.
Excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to translate operational challenges into technical solutions.
Experience building products from scratch and taking them into production.

Bonus points if you have:
Experience at an HR technology company, Work OS platform, or identity provider,
Experience with HRIS, ATS, compensation, workforce planning tools.
Experience building AI-powered products or internal tooling.
Experience working closely with People or Operations teams.

What you'll do
In one sentence:
Build AI-powered People systems that make Lovable run better — and create products that can graduate from internal tools to customer-facing features.
Examples include:
Partner with the People team to identify, scope, and ship AI-powered internal products.
Build integrations with HR systems (HiBob, Ashby, etc.), ATS platforms, and identity providers.
Design secure systems with robust role-based permissions and access controls.
Develop predictive and diagnostic models (workforce trends, hiring capacity, retention risks, compensation dynamics).
Create canonical datasets and source-of-truth models for hiring, headcount, compensation, organizational design, and workforce planning.
Data governance — source-of-truth logic, naming conventions, ownership.
Own products end-to-end—from research and design through implementation, deployment, and iteration.
Translate operational challenges into elegant technical solutions.
Build systems that meet legal and compliance requirements for handling sensitive employee data.
Work closely with other AI Ops Engineers, sharing building blocks, patterns, and learnings across Lovable's functions.
Build AI agents, workflows, dashboards, and decision-support tools that help leaders make better decisions.

Our tech stack
We're building with tools that both humans and AI love.
Languages: TypeScript, Python, Go
AI: OpenAI, Anthropic, MCP, AI Agents
Business Systems: HiBob, Ashby, Okta
Infrastructure: Cloudflare, PostgreSQL, Temporal

jobs.description:
🚀 Challenge the Impossible​ ​
 
About Beyond Gravity
Beyond Gravity, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, is the first space company to combine a startup mindset, agility, speed and innovation with decades of experience and proven quality. Approximately 1800 employees at 12 locations in six countries (Switzerland, Sweden, Austria, USA, Finland and Portugal) develop and manufacture products for satellites and launch vehicles with the goal of advancing humankind and enabling the exploration of the world and beyond. Beyond Gravity is the preferred supplier of structures for all types of launch vehicles and a leading provider of selected satellite products and constellation solutions in the New Space sector. In 2024, the company generated a revenue of around CHF 359 million. More information at: www.beyondgravity.com
 
Your crew

Join a highly collaborative, cross-functional team at the heart of Beyond Gravity’s Electronics business. Working closely with Engineering, Product Management, Programs, Production and other functions, you will contribute to the development of satellite onboard systems, platform and payload products as well as ground electronics products.
As an Electronics System Engineer, you will work at system and architectural level, providing system engineering expertise for electronics hardware systems, embedded processing systems and platform and payload solutions across development projects and series production programs in the satellite electronic solutions domain.
This is a role with significant development potential. You will have the opportunity to take increasing ownership, broaden your technical expertise and grow towards more advanced system engineering responsibilities over time.
 
Your mission

The Electronics System Engineer is responsible for:
Take ownership of your scope and bring assigned tasks to completion, involving more senior colleagues when needed.
Develop and maintain satellite onboard systems, platform and payload products as well as ground electronics products at system and architectural level.
Analyse and understand internal and external customer requirements and translate them into system-level requirements and technical solutions.
Break down system requirements into subsystem and module requirements and establish corresponding design requirements.
Develop technical concepts and system designs appropriate to customer and project needs, considering cost, time, quality, performance and technical feasibility.
Perform and/or assess system-level analyses, including performance, radiation, structural, EMC, reliability, FDIR and HW/FPGA/SW interaction analyses.
Coordinate development activities with other teams and disciplines to ensure complete and intended implementation of the system.
Plan and execute your own activities, monitor progress against schedule and budget, and raise awareness of risks and blocking points.
Support bidding and proposal activities through technical descriptions, concept work, cost and schedule estimates and risk and opportunity assessments.
Contribute to continuous improvement of products, technologies, processes and ways of working, challenging established solutions where appropriate.
Interact with customers, suppliers and external stakeholders within your area of responsibility and provide technical know-how to support successful project execution.
Maintain and develop system-level documentation and ensure compliance with established development processes and standards.

 
Most important outputs:
Robust and efficient system solutions that meet customer and project requirements.
Successful delivery of system engineering activities within agreed scope, quality, schedule and budget.
Continuous development of products, technologies and engineering methods.

 
Your story

We are looking for a technically curious and solution-oriented System Engineer with a strong interest in satellite electronics and system engineering. You take ownership of your work, are comfortable working independently and enjoy finding solutions to complex technical challenges.
You have a collaborative mindset and enjoy working across disciplines, with the ability to communicate clearly with colleagues, customers and external partners. You are motivated by continuous learning and want to develop your expertise and responsibility over time.
This role is a great opportunity for someone with strong potential to grow towards more advanced system engineering responsibilities and, in time, a Senior System Engineer role.
 
Must-haves:
M.Sc. in Electrical, Software or Aerospace Engineering, or corresponding experience.
Experience or good knowledge in system engineering, electronics or embedded systems, preferably within the space industry.
Understanding of requirements engineering, functional decomposition and system design.
Ability to perform or assess system-level analyses and understand HW/FPGA/SW interactions.
Ability to work independently, take ownership and deliver within agreed scope, schedule and budget.
Strong collaboration and communication skills.
Structured and solution-oriented approach to technical challenges and risk.
Fluent English, written and spoken.

 
Nice to have’s:
Experience with satellite onboard systems, platform and payload products or ground electronics.
Knowledge of FPGA, hardware, RF, signal processing or embedded systems.
Experience with tools such as MATLAB, DOORS, PSA, FMECA, DOSRAD or Reliability.
Knowledge of ECSS, agile methods or model-based systems engineering.
Experience with technical coordination, customer interaction or proposal work.
Knowledge of product roadmaps and current technology trends.

 
Why Beyond Gravity
 
To work in a growing high technology company with career opportunities within the site or internationally.
You will be a part of an engaged team with the ambition to innovate space!
We offer a hybrid work situation, high flexibility and autonomy, and a great team to develop and have fun with!

 
🌌Are you ready for lift-off?​
Our core values - Passionate, Together, and Curious - transform challenges into opportunities. Embark on a journey to transcend the ordinary with us. We‘re actively reviewing candidates and will promptly select the ideal fit for our team.​
​Beyond Gravity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.
